info.description: TOUCHE COMMERCE trade management API. Stage 1A exposes identity (server-side sessions), multi-company membership and tenant isolation on top of the Stage 0 foundation.
info.title: TOUCHE COMMERCE API

post.description: Verifies the credentials with Argon2id, applies the login rate limit and creates a server-side session. The opaque session token is delivered in an HttpOnly cookie; the body never contains the token or the password hash. All failures return the same 401 message so account existence is not revealed. The active company is auto-selected only when the user has exactly one active membership.
post.summary: Sign in and open a server-side session

post.description: Revokes the session row immediately (the cookie alone would be useless afterwards) and clears the cookie. Requires the CSRF header.
post.summary: Revoke the current session

get.description: Re-validates the session and the active membership on every call and returns the CSRF token the client must send on state-changing requests.
get.summary: Current user, active company and memberships

get.description: Returns only companies with an active membership for the caller, together with the role and permissions held in each. The list is derived from the database on every request, so a revoked membership disappears immediately.
get.summary: Companies the signed-in user may access

get.description: Cursor-paginated, newest first. Filters are bound to the cursor: reusing a cursor with a different filter set is rejected with 422 instead of returning a misleading page.

post.summary: Create a counterparty

patch.description: Requires If-Match with the ETag from the last read. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT including the current ETag; a missing header returns 428 PRECONDITION_REQUIRED. Unknown fields (for example status) are rejected.

200.description: Updated; the new ETag is returned.

get.description: Deal counts by status, open pipeline per currency, catalogue/CRM totals and the most recent deals and audit activity. All values come from the database in one transaction; nothing is inferred in the browser.
get.summary: Trade dashboard for the active company

get.description: Cursor-paginated, newest first. Every row carries its total value computed from the deal lines, so a table never has to sum client-side.

post.description: Creates the deal, every line, the initial DRAFT history entry and the audit record in one transaction. A deal cannot reference a counterparty or product belonging to another company (composite foreign keys plus RLS).
post.summary: Create a deal with its lines

get.summary: Read one deal with lines, history and allowed transitions

patch.description: Header fields only: title, counterparty, currency, expected close date and notes. Sending status is rejected with 422 because status changes belong to the transition endpoint. Closed deals cannot be edited. Lines are immutable.

200.description: Updated; the new ETag is returned.

409.description: Closed deal, version or key conflict.

post.description: Requires Idempotency-Key. The optional If-Match header adds optimistic concurrency on top of row locking. The deal update, the deal_transition history row and the audit row commit in one transaction.

200.description: Transition accepted; the new ETag is returned.

409.description: INVALID_TRANSITION, TRANSITION_DISABLED, ALREADY_WON, VERSION_CONFLICT, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT or IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS.

post.summary: Move a deal through the state machine

get.description: Cursor-paginated, newest recording first. Filter by the currency pair. No endpoint returns a 'current' rate: pricing always refers to a stored snapshot so a landed cost stays reproducible.

post.description: Stores one sourced observation. The pair and effective time are unique per company, so recording the same observation twice is a 409 instead of a duplicate rate that could be picked arbitrarily.
post.summary: Record an FX snapshot

get.description: Returns 200 as soon as the API process can serve HTTP. It deliberately performs no database, cache or network I/O so a dependency outage cannot cause the orchestrator to kill a healthy process.
Verifies that required dependencies are usable. Currently checks the PostgreSQL connection using the runtime role. Returns 503 with the standard error envelope when a dependency is unavailable.
Cursor-paginated, newest first. The summary carries landed total, sales total and gross margin so a comparison table needs no extra call.

post.description: Converts the quote into the target currency using an explicit FX snapshot, allocates every cost component (ORDER pro-rata by purchase value, LINE to its product) and derives selling prices from exactly one of margin or markup. The inputs and the rounded results are stored together.

400.description: Missing FX snapshot, unpriced line or invalid component.

post.summary: Price a supplier quote (landed cost + selling price)

get.summary: Read one scenario with inputs, results and components

put.description: Replaces the cost components and reruns the engine for the same supplier quote. A scenario is bound to its quote: repointing it is a 400, not a silent rewrite of history.

200.description: Recalculated; the new ETag is returned.

put.summary: Recalculate a scenario with new inputs (If-Match required)

get.description: Cursor-paginated catalogue, newest first; search matches SKU and name.

post.summary: Create a product

200.description: Updated; the new ETag is returned.

get.description: Cursor-paginated, newest first. Each row carries its line and quote counts so a comparison table never has to fan out per row.

post.description: Every supplier receives its own RFQ with the same lines, created in one transaction. A buyer counterparty is rejected: an RFQ is addressed to a supplier. References are generated per RFQ.
post.summary: Create one RFQ per supplier

get.summary: Read one RFQ with lines, quotes and prepared revisions

patch.description: Draft and prepared RFQs are editable. Editing a prepared RFQ returns it to DRAFT and opens the next revision, so the prepared snapshot stays intact. Status is not writable here: use the transitions endpoint.

200.description: Updated; the new ETag is returned.

post.description: The quote inherits its supplier, deal and line descriptions from the RFQ. Only a SENT (or re-quoted RESPONDED) RFQ accepts a quote, and only one received quote may be active at a time: later prices are revisions.

400.description: Unknown product, invalid Incoterm or missing key.

409.description: RFQ not sent, or a quote is already active.

post.summary: Record a supplier's quote against a sent RFQ

get.description: Prepared snapshots are append-only; this returns the stored JSON as written.

post.description: Requires Idempotency-Key. PREPARED writes an immutable revision snapshot; SENT requires channel and evidence; CANCELLED requires a reason.

200.description: Transition accepted; the new ETag is returned.

post.summary: Move an RFQ through its lifecycle

get.description: Cursor-paginated, newest first. Each row includes the scenario status so a reviewer can see whether the underlying inputs were verified.

post.description: Prices are copied from the scenario's stored results, so the quote matches the calculation that was reviewed. A supplier counterparty cannot be a customer. The new quote starts in DRAFT.
post.summary: Draft a sales quote from a pricing scenario

get.summary: Read one sales quote with lines, revisions and allowed actions

post.description: Requires the ``finance.approve`` permission (traders and admins never hold it) and refuses the submitter, so approval is always a second pair of eyes.

200.description: Approved; the new ETag is returned.

post.summary: Approve a submitted quote (finance.approve)

post.description: A rejection explains itself: the reason is stored and audited.

200.description: Rejected; the new ETag is returned.

post.summary: Reject a submitted quote (finance.approve)

post.description: The new revision starts in DRAFT, carries the next revision number and supersedes the previous row. Prices are re-read from the pricing scenario.
post.summary: Open a new revision of an approved, rejected or withdrawn quote

get.summary: Read a stored sales quote revision snapshot

post.description: Only a scenario with VERIFIED_INPUTS may be submitted: an estimate can be drafted and discussed, never approved as if it were verified.

200.description: Submitted; the new ETag is returned.

409.description: Invalid transition, unverified scenario or version conflict.

post.summary: Submit a draft for approval (If-Match + Idempotency-Key required)

post.description: Withdrawal is a dead end: an approved quote cannot be withdrawn, it is superseded by a new revision instead, so the approval trail stays intact.

200.description: Withdrawn; the new ETag is returned.

post.summary: Withdraw a draft or submitted quote (If-Match required)

post.description: Requires a CSRF header and an active membership for the requested company. The company id supplied by the client is only used as a lookup key: an unauthorised id returns 403 and writes an ACCESS_DENIED audit record. On success the session token and CSRF token are rotated and the absolute expiry is preserved.

403.description: No membership, CSRF or origin rejected.

post.summary: Select the active company and rotate the session token

get.description: Cursor-paginated by receipt time, newest first. Superseded revisions stay visible with their ``superseded_by_quote_id`` set, so a price history is never lost.

get.summary: Read one supplier quote with lines and revisions

post.description: Creates a new quote row that supersedes the given one. The previous revision is never modified, so both prices remain readable and only the newest revision can be priced.

409.description: Not received, already superseded or version conflict.

post.summary: Record a new revision of a supplier quote (If-Match required)

get.summary: Read a stored quote revision snapshot

post.description: A withdrawn quote keeps its data and revision history but can no longer be priced; a reason is required and recorded in the audit trail.

200.description: Withdrawn; the new ETag is returned.

post.summary: Withdraw a received quote (If-Match required)
